review_scope: Checked the prespecified multi-partner target, support graph invariants, all four source-level primary differences and fixed-checkpoint AUC.
Checked both fixed FW/WF donor assignments and all 199 complete-code relabeling references.
Checked independent raw-statistic and bounded execution audit outputs, terminal accounting and figure visual QA.
Checked every absolute local link in the final report.

findings.interpretation: The multi-partner target removes the one-to-one shortcut, but the path-alignment contrast is not directionally stable across sources.
Single-resource accuracy is much higher than the requirement to get both partners of a fixed resource correct.
Offline donor recombination exceeds the complete-code relabel reference, but this is not autonomous composition.

limitations: Four inherited initialization sources; panels, directions, masks and photo rows are nested repeats.
The two arms differ in five concrete edges as well as target path distribution; path count is not isolated.
The target is a controlled symbolic location task, not a reconstruction of human ecology; private visual/world knowledge is inherited.
Full-code relabeling preserves full-message behavior and is a post-training descriptive reference.
The bounded audit does not replay every gradient and Adam state transition.
The finite 199-reference tail resolution is descriptive, not a four-source significance test.
next_step: Add a task-level multi-partner payoff and an equal-information whole-code control; then compare fixed and rotating partners under the same target graph.

figure_visual_qa.method: PIL raster dimension/finite/nonwhite checks plus direct visual inspection with view_image
